sentences.en: Cambridge professor says that a change in drinking habits was the reason for the Industrial Revolution in Britain, Anjana Ahuja reports
sentences.zh: 剑桥教授表示,饮酒习惯的改变是英国工业革命的原因,Anjana Ahuja 报道

sentences.zh: A. 艾伦·麦克法兰（A. Alan Macfarlane）是剑桥大学国王学院的人类学教授,和其他历史学家一样,花了数十年的时间来解开工业革命的谜团。

sentences.en: Why did this particular Big Bangthe world-changing birth of industry - happen in Britain?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个特殊的大爆炸——改变世界的工业诞生——发生在英国？

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: B. Macfarlane compares the puzzle to a combination lock.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: "There are about 20 different factors and all of them need to be present before the revolution can happen”, he says.
sentences.zh: “大约有 20 个不同的因素,所有这些因素都需要在革命发生之前出现”,他说。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: For industry to take off, there needs to be the technology and power to drive factories, large urban populations to provide cheap labour, easy transport to move goods around, an affluent middle-class willing to buy mass-produced objects, a market-driven economy and a political system that allows this to happen.
sentences.zh: 工业要腾飞,需要有技术和动力来驱动工厂、大量城市人口提供廉价劳动力、方便的运输来运送货物、富裕的中产阶级愿意购买大规模生产的物品、市场驱动的经济和允许这一切发生的政治体系。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: While this was the case for England, other nations, such as Japan, the Netherlands, and France also met some of these criteria but were not industrializing.
sentences.zh: 虽然英国就是这种情况,但日本、荷兰和法国等其他国家也满足了其中一些标准,但没有实现工业化。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: ‘All these factors must have been necessary but not sufficient to cause the revolution,’ says Macfarlane.
sentences.zh: “所有这些因素必定是必要的,但不足以引发革命,”麦克法兰说。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: 'After all, Holland had everything except coal, while China also had many of these factors.
sentences.zh: ‘毕竟荷兰什么都有,除了煤炭,而中国也有很多这样的因素。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Most historians are convinced there are one or two missing factors that you need to open the lock. '
sentences.zh: 大多数历史学家相信,打开锁需要一两个缺失的因素。 '

sentences.en: The antiseptic properties of tannin, the active ingredient in tea, and of hops in beer – plus the fact that both are made with boiled water - allowed urban communities to flourish at close quarters without succumbing to water-borne diseases such as dysentery.
sentences.zh: 茶中的活性成分单宁和啤酒中的啤酒花的防腐特性——再加上两者都是用开水制成的——使得城市社区能够在近距离繁荣发展,而不会死于水传播疾病,例如痢疾。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.zh: 麦克法兰的论点得到了知名人士的支持 - 杰出的医学历史学家罗伊·波特最近对他的研究发表了积极的评价

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；“be + 过去分词”强调动作的承受者。

sentences.en: D. Macfarlane had wondered for a long time how the Industrial Revolution came about.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Historians had alighted on one interesting factor around the mid-18th century that required explanation.
sentences.zh: 历史学家在 18 世纪中叶发现了一个需要解释的有趣因素。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Between about 1650 and 1740, the population in Britain was static.
sentences.zh: 大约在 1650 年至 1740 年间,英国的人口是静态的。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: But then there was a burst in population growth.
sentences.zh: 但随后人口急剧增长。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Macfarlane says: ‘The infant mortality rate halved in the space of 20 years, and this happened in both rural areas and cities and across all classes.
sentences.zh: 麦克法兰说：“婴儿死亡率在 20 年内减半,这发生在农村地区和城市以及各个阶层。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: People suggested four possible causes.
sentences.zh: 人们提出了四种可能的原因。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Was there a sudden change in the viruses and bacteria around? Unlikely.
sentences.zh: 周围的病毒和细菌是不是突然发生了变化？不太可能。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Was there a revolution in medical science?
sentences.zh: 医学有革命吗？

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: But this was a century before Lister's revolution*.
sentences.zh: 但这是李斯特革命*前的一个世纪。

sentences.en: Was there a change in environmental conditions?

sentences.en: There were improvements in agriculture that wiped out malaria, but these were small gains.
sentences.zh: 农业取得了进步,消灭了疟疾,但这些成果很小。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Sanitation did not become widespread until the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 卫生设施直到 19 世纪才普及。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.zh: 解释儿童死亡人数突然减少的努力似乎一片空白。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: E. This population burst seemed to happen at just the right time to provide labour for the Industrial Revolution.

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；to do 常表示目的、结果或对前面内容的补充。

sentences.en: ‘When you start moving towards an industrial revolution, it is economically efficient to have people living close together' says Macfarlane.
sentences.zh: “当你开始走向工业革命时,让人们住在一起在经济上是有效的,”麦克法兰说。

sentences.en: Some digging around in historical records revealed that there was a change in the incidence of water-borne disease at that time, especially dysentery.
sentences.zh: 一些历史记录的挖掘表明,当时水传播疾病的发病率发生了变化,特别是痢疾。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Macfarlane deduced that whatever the British were drinking must have been important in regulating disease.
sentences.zh: 麦克法兰推断,无论英国人喝什么,一定对调节疾病很重要。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: He says, "We drank beer. For a long time, the English were protected by the strong antibacterial agent in hops, which were added to help preserve the beer. But in the late 17 th century a tax was introduced on malt, the basic ingredient of beer. The poor turned to water and gin and in the 1720s the mortality rate began to rise again. Then it suddenly dropped again. What caused this?".
sentences.zh: 他说,“我们喝啤酒。很长一段时间,英国人受到啤酒花中强效抗菌剂的保护,添加啤酒花是为了帮助保存啤酒。但在 17 世纪末,对啤酒的基本成分麦芽征税。穷人转向水和杜松子酒,在 1720 年代,死亡率开始再次上升。然后又突然下降。这是什么原因造成的？”。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Could it be the prevalence of tea in their culture?
sentences.zh: 难道是因为茶在他们的文化中盛行？

sentences.en: Macfarlane then noted that the history of tea in Britain provided an extraordinary coincidence of dates.
sentences.zh: 麦克法兰随后指出,英国的茶叶历史提供了一个非同寻常的日期巧合。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Tea was relatively expensive until Britain started a direct clipper trade with China in the early 18th century.
sentences.zh: 在英国于 18 世纪初开始与中国进行直接快船贸易之前,茶叶相对昂贵。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: By the 1740s, about the time that infant mortality was dipping, the drink was common.
sentences.zh: 到了 1740 年代,大约在婴儿死亡率下降的时候,这种饮料已经很常见了。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；按主语、谓语和宾语／表语的顺序先抓句子主干。

sentences.en: Macfarlane guessed that the fact that water had to be boiled, together with the stomach-purifying properties of tea meant that the breast milk provided by mothers was healthier than it had ever been.
sentences.zh: 麦克法兰猜测,水必须煮沸,再加上茶具有净化胃的特性,这意味着母亲提供的母乳比以往任何时候都更健康。

grammar.type: 被动语态 + 不定式结构

sentences.en: No other European nation sipped tea like the British, which, by Macfarlane's logic, pushed these other countries out of contention for the revolution.
sentences.zh: 没有其他欧洲国家像英国人那样喝茶,按照麦克法兰的逻辑,英国人将这些其他国家排除在了革命的竞争之外。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；which/who/where 引导的部分用来补充说明前面的名词。

sentences.en: G. But, if tea is a factor in the combination lock, why didn't Japan forge ahead in a tea-soaked industrial revolution of its own?
sentences.zh: G. 但是,如果茶是密码锁的一个因素,为什么日本没有推进自己的茶工业革命呢？

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: Macfarlane notes that even though 17th-century Japan had large cities, high literacy rates, even a futures market, it had turned its back on the essence of any work-based revolution by giving up labour-saving devices such as animals, afraid that they would put people out of work.
sentences.zh: 麦克法兰指出,尽管 17 世纪的日本拥有大城市、高识字率,甚至还有期货市场,但它放弃了动物等节省劳动力的设备,从而背弃了任何以工作为基础的革命的本质,担心它们会让人们失业。

grammar.note: 先抓主句主干；连词引出时间、原因、条件或让步关系。

sentences.en: So, the nation that we now think of as one of the most technologically advanced entered the 19th century having 'abandoned the wheel'.
sentences.zh: 因此,我们现在认为是技术最先进的国家之一进入了 19 世纪,“放弃了车轮”。
